Scope: infrastructure over about 6.5 km² of the Fourth Industrial City in Riyadh: roads and tunnels, electrical, telecom, ICT and security networks, potable water and fire-fighting, irrigation, sewage and stormwater networks, and sewage and stormwater pumping stations.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 32.9% against 32.9% planned, the weekly report now puts the project level with the plan (SPI 1.00), from 2.1% behind last week. It gained 2.9% this week against 0.7% planned, four times the weekly plan. About half of the gain came from procurement (3,331 of 6,752 earned man-hours), as the first deliveries of telecom ducts, street-lighting poles and cable and precast curbs were recorded; earthworks added 1,524 man-hours after three weeks without change. The zone network works are still far behind (12.8% against 28.8% planned), and the P6 update still finishes the project 225 days late, so being level with the plan does not mean the delay has been recovered.

The schedule still finishes the project about seven months late. The P6 update uploaded this week (data date 23-Nov-2026) finishes the project on 10-Jan-2029, 225 days after the contract completion date of 30-May-2028 (last week: 14-Jan-2029, −229 days). The weekly report gives the same date. In P6 the roads finish on 25-Apr-2027 and the MV network on 28-Oct-2027, against the contract milestone of 30-Sep-2026 for MV and road works.

Clash with Green Riyadh servicesContractor / Green RiyadhAn air vent and cathodic protection on Road C8 clash with the works. Coordination with Green Riyadh's contractor is ongoing to get drawings and price the diversion. Rated critical; still in progress, with a target of 30-Nov-2026.

Progress behind planContractorProgress lags the schedule because of the master plan change (Wadi Al-Sulai) and the equipment shortage at the start. Most shop drawings are done, and equipment and network crews were increased. Rated critical; status: monitoring.
SEC cable clashes (closed)Contractor / SECBoth clashes are closed. On Road C2 the contractor appointed by SEC has started and is supporting the high-voltage cables. On Road C8 a start-of-work record was signed with SEC's contractor (Pillar).

Delay reasons stated in the report: the master layout changed after the Wadi Al-Sulai redesign, which changed the design of all networks; and equipment was short at the start of the project.

Data notes

This report uses the two files uploaded for 23-Nov-2026 (the weekly report workbook and the P6 update) and, for this-week values, the 16-Nov-2026 files. No progress presentation, quantities and procurement file, MASTER LOG, material tracking sheet or invoice backup was uploaded this week. Every progress percentage is physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. There is no S-curve section: the workbook's Physical-Chart Data sheet is empty.

  • The week number, 51, is the contract week stated on the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 51 of 130"); it also equals the whole weeks from site handover (30-Nov-2025) to the data date (358 days).
  • The workbook also gives a cost-based progress figure, labelled as actual progress in places. This report does not use it.
  • Physical progress jumped by 2.9% (6,752 man-hours) in one week, four times the weekly plan, and the total now sits just 0.01% above the plan. About half of the gain (3,331 man-hours) is procurement, credited as the telecom network and street-lighting poles went from 0% to 100% delivered in a single week, while the MIR count stayed at 113 issued and 113 closed. Earthworks gained 1,524 man-hours after three weeks without change. These earned man-hours should be checked against delivery records and inspections before the on-plan figure is accepted.
  • The forecast finish agrees between the P6 update, the P6 extract in the lower table of the Progress sheet and the General Information sheet (10-Jan-2029, −225 days), but the upper table of the Progress sheet again carries last week's values (14-Jan-2029, −229 days). The Milestones sheet still shows no delay on any milestone.
  • Mobilisation finished on 29-Dec-2025 according to P6, but on 30-Mar-2026 according to the weekly report.
  • The Conclusion sheet was restructured this week. It dropped the MV and LV rows; it splits street lighting into poles (4 installed) and cable (0 m installed), against 180 m of street lighting last week; and it adds the asphalt wearing course (32,880 m³, against 33,040.86 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet), sewage manholes, open-channel excavation (183,180.23 m³, 22,577.7 m³ done) and riprap (43,858.6 m², 6,476.19 m² done). The Major Quantities sheet lists only 13,350 m³ of channel excavation and 11,000 m² of riprap, with nothing done. The second "fill" line (3,947,936 m³ total, 121,000 m³ done) is still there.
  • On the Major Quantities sheet the delivered quantities of the storm, sewage, potable water and irrigation networks now show #REF!; this report uses the delivered quantities on the Conclusion sheet.
  • Tunnel 01 slab concrete is still 1,535 m³ against 1,402.72 m³ in the BOQ (109%). Tunnel 01 concrete is 5,590 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet but 4,055 m³ on the Major sheet, and box culvert concrete (6,274 m³) is measured against 10,940.61 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet but 3,870 m³ on the Major sheet (162%).
  • Quality: no count on the Quality-Stat sheet changed this week, and its inspection requests still show 490 issued but 1,687 closed and 236 pending.
  • Safety: man-hours this week are 17,880 for the fourth week running. Cumulative man-hours now rise with the weekly figure, but the cumulative induction and toolbox-talk counts stay at 74 and 504 although the sheet records 3 inductions and 9 toolbox talks this week.
  • Invoices: the workbook lists 9 invoices, 86,818,263 SAR gross, none approved by the MODON PM and none paid. The contract value of 445,000,000 SAR is called "including VAT" on the Conclusion sheet but "excluding VAT" in the bill breakdown.
  • Activity counts differ: the Weekly Progress Report sheet gives 9,903 activities (2,602 completed, 914 in progress, 6,387 not started), the P6 update 8,625 (1,872, 576 and 6,177).
  • Issues: the Issues sheet still lists the SEC clash as active, with a closure date of 30-Apr-2026 that has passed, while the issue log closed it on 30-Oct-2026. The issue log's targets for the Green Riyadh, ARAMCO and procurement issues (30-Nov-2026) fall within the coming week.
  • Procurement: the workbook's Proc. Stat summary lists only GRP pipes and fittings (28,765 units), not all materials.
  • Several summary panels still show #REF! or #DIV/0! errors.
  • Photos: the six used are GPS-stamped 19–23 Nov 2026. Not used: the base course photo on RD-L-16 (similar to the RD-C-6 photo) and the tunnel roof insulation photo (no stamp). The Weekly Photos sheet calls the RD-C-6 photo "RD-C-66".
